archetypes.name: migration-completeness
archetypes.rationale: A sh-to-py migration that deletes 10 shell scripts and retargets callers is high-risk for stale references; callers not shown in the diff may still invoke the deleted paths, causing silent runtime failures in the /implement and /design orchestration paths.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit whether any files not updated in this diff still reference the retired shell scripts: clarify-state.sh, clarify-comment-post.sh, clarify-label.sh, test-clarify-state.sh, test-clarify-comment.sh, and their .md counterparts. Focus on hooks/hooks.json, CI workflow YAML, skills/implement/SKILL.md, skills/design/SKILL.md, scripts/test-plan-block.sh, scripts/get-issue-context.sh, .claude/rules/gh-body-file.md, and any other SKILL.md or scripts/ paths that might invoke clarify helpers. Also check whether both Makefile targets test-clarify-state and test-clarify-comment now running the identical pytest invocation could create a CI blind spot where a regression in only the former or latter logical test group passes undetected. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: init-order
archetypes.rationale: In the bash scripts larch_quiet_init ran before any argument parsing; in the Python CLI mains quiet_init is called after _parse_state_args, so argparse-driven SystemExit paths (--help, missing required args) exit before the quiet machinery is initialized, which may break callers relying on a specific output contract for those exit paths.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the initialization ordering in clarify_state_main, clarify_comment_post_main, and clarify_label_main: each calls logging_util.quiet_init() only after _parse_state_args/_parse_comment_args/_parse_label_args succeed, but those parse helpers raise SystemExit directly on --help or missing-arg errors, before quiet_init is called. Determine whether this ordering matches the retired shell helpers' contract for the same error conditions, focusing on whether fd-3 machine-readable KVs are ever expected for --help or missing-required-arg exits. Also evaluate whether the three-layer validation pattern (argparse required-arg check, _validate_positive_issue_for_cli, then domain-level _ensure_positive_text) can produce divergent exit codes or error messages for the same invalid input, and whether _parse_state_args returning argparse.Namespace | None in its type annotation but never actually returning None makes the subsequent args is None guards dead code with any downstream risk. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
